title: General Biology II
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 100L General Biology II curriculum (the diversity-of-life continuation of General Biology I): principles of classification, viruses, kingdoms Monera/Protista/Fungi/Plantae/Animalia, basic ecology, and introductory Mendelian genetics and evolution.

questions.question: Who is widely regarded as the father of modern taxonomy for developing the binomial system of nomenclature?
questions.explanation: Carl Linnaeus developed the two-name (genus + species) system of naming organisms that is still used today.

questions.question: Arrange the following taxonomic ranks from the broadest to the most specific: Class, Family, Genus, Kingdom, Order, Phylum, Species.
options: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Family, Order, Genus, Species
Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum, Kingdom reversed as broadest first
Phylum, Kingdom, Class, Family, Order, Genus, Species
questions.correct_answer: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
questions.explanation: The standard taxonomic hierarchy from broadest to most specific is Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correctly formatted binomial scientific name?
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature the genus name is capitalised and the species name is lowercase, both conventionally italicised, e.g. Panthera leo.

questions.question: A named taxonomic group at any level of the classification hierarchy (e.g. a species, genus, or family) is referred to as a:
questions.explanation: A taxon is the general term for a unit of classification at any rank in the taxonomic hierarchy.

questions.question: The modern three-domain system of classification, proposed by Carl Woese, groups all living organisms into:
questions.explanation: The three-domain system separates prokaryotes into Bacteria and Archaea, with all eukaryotic organisms placed in domain Eukarya.

questions.question: Viruses are described as obligate intracellular parasites because they:
options: Can only replicate by taking over the metabolic machinery of a living host cell
Can photosynthesize only inside a host
questions.correct_answer: Can only replicate by taking over the metabolic machinery of a living host cell
questions.explanation: Viruses lack the machinery for independent metabolism and reproduction, so they must infect a host cell and hijack its ribosomes and enzymes to replicate.

questions.question: The protein shell that encloses and protects a virus's genetic material is called the:
questions.explanation: The capsid is the protein coat, made of subunits called capsomeres, that surrounds the viral genome.

questions.question: A virus that specifically infects and replicates within bacterial cells is called a:
questions.explanation: Bacteriophages (or 'phages') are viruses that infect bacteria, injecting their genetic material into the bacterial cell.

questions.question: Why do biologists consider viruses to occupy a unique position between living and non-living things?
options: They show properties of life such as reproduction and mutation only inside a host cell, but are metabolically inert outside one
They are entirely non-living and cannot mutate at all
They can grow and carry out independent respiration outside a host
They have cellular structure identical to bacteria
questions.correct_answer: They show properties of life such as reproduction and mutation only inside a host cell, but are metabolically inert outside one
questions.explanation: Outside a host, a virus is essentially an inert particle; it only displays hallmarks of life such as replication and mutation once inside a living cell.

questions.question: Bacteria are classified as prokaryotes mainly because their cells:
options: Lack a membrane-bound nucleus and most membrane-bound organelles
questions.correct_answer: Lack a membrane-bound nucleus and most membrane-bound organelles
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells, such as bacteria, have their genetic material free in the cytoplasm rather than enclosed in a nuclear envelope.

questions.question: The Gram staining technique differentiates bacteria mainly on the basis of differences in their:
options: Cell wall peptidoglycan composition and thickness
questions.correct_answer: Cell wall peptidoglycan composition and thickness
questions.explanation: Gram staining exploits the fact that Gram-positive bacteria have a thick peptidoglycan layer that retains crystal violet dye, while Gram-negative bacteria have a thin layer and lose the stain.

questions.question: Gram-positive bacteria retain the crystal violet stain during Gram staining mainly because they have a:
options: Thin peptidoglycan cell wall with an outer membrane
Cell wall made of cellulose only
questions.explanation: The thick peptidoglycan layer of Gram-positive bacteria traps the crystal violet-iodine complex, so the cells stain purple.

questions.question: Bacteria (such as cyanobacteria) that manufacture their own food using light energy are described as:
questions.explanation: Photoautotrophic bacteria, like cyanobacteria, use light energy to synthesise organic compounds from carbon dioxide and water.

questions.question: The most common form of asexual reproduction in bacteria is:
questions.explanation: Bacteria typically reproduce asexually by binary fission, in which a single cell divides into two genetically identical daughter cells.

questions.question: Members of Kingdom Protista are best generally described as organisms that are:
questions.explanation: Protists are a diverse eukaryotic group, predominantly unicellular, that do not fit neatly into the plant, animal, or fungal kingdoms.

questions.question: Amoeba moves and captures food using temporary cytoplasmic extensions called:
questions.explanation: Amoeba extends 'false feet' (pseudopodia) from its cytoplasm to move and engulf food particles by phagocytosis.

questions.question: Paramecium, a ciliate protist, moves through water mainly by beating numerous short hair-like structures called:
questions.explanation: Paramecium is covered in cilia whose coordinated beating propels the organism through its aquatic environment.

questions.question: Malaria in humans is caused by a protozoan parasite of which genus?
questions.explanation: Plasmodium species, transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes, are the protozoan parasites responsible for malaria.

questions.question: Algae are placed in Kingdom Protista (rather than Kingdom Plantae) mainly because they:
options: Are eukaryotic, photosynthetic organisms that lack true roots, stems, and leaves
Have true vascular tissue like ferns
questions.correct_answer: Are eukaryotic, photosynthetic organisms that lack true roots, stems, and leaves
questions.explanation: Although algae photosynthesize like plants, they lack the specialised true tissues and organs (roots, stems, leaves) that define Kingdom Plantae, so they are classified as protists.

questions.question: Fungal cell walls are primarily composed of which structural polysaccharide?
questions.explanation: Unlike plant cell walls (cellulose) or bacterial cell walls (peptidoglycan), fungal cell walls are made largely of chitin.

questions.question: Fungi obtain their nutrition mainly by:
options: Secreting digestive enzymes onto organic matter and absorbing the digested products
Ingesting whole food particles by phagocytosis
questions.correct_answer: Secreting digestive enzymes onto organic matter and absorbing the digested products
questions.explanation: Fungi are heterotrophic decomposers that digest food externally by secreting enzymes, then absorb the resulting nutrients (saprophytic nutrition).

questions.question: The thread-like filaments that make up the vegetative body of most fungi are called:
questions.explanation: A fungal body (mycelium) is composed of a network of thread-like filaments called hyphae.

questions.question: A lichen is best described as:
options: A mutualistic association between a fungus and a photosynthetic alga or cyanobacterium
A parasitic fungus that kills its plant host
questions.correct_answer: A mutualistic association between a fungus and a photosynthetic alga or cyanobacterium
questions.explanation: In a lichen, the fungal partner provides structure and absorbs water/minerals while the algal or cyanobacterial partner provides food through photosynthesis.

questions.question: Common mushrooms, with their characteristic gilled fruiting bodies, belong to which fungal phylum?
questions.explanation: Mushrooms are club fungi (Basidiomycota), named for the basidium, the club-shaped structure on which spores are produced.

questions.question: Bryophytes (e.g. mosses) are described as non-vascular plants because they:
options: Lack specialised xylem and phloem tissues for conducting water and nutrients
Have true roots but no leaves
questions.correct_answer: Lack specialised xylem and phloem tissues for conducting water and nutrients
questions.explanation: Bryophytes have no true vascular tissue, which limits their size and restricts them to moist habitats where water can move by diffusion and capillarity.

questions.question: In the life cycle of a typical moss, the dominant, longer-lived generation is the:
questions.explanation: In bryophytes, unlike in vascular plants, the haploid gametophyte is the dominant, photosynthetic generation, with the sporophyte remaining attached to and dependent on it.

questions.question: Ferns, which reproduce by spores and possess true vascular tissue but no seeds, belong to the plant group:
questions.explanation: Ferns are seedless vascular plants (Pteridophyta) that disperse via spores rather than seeds.

questions.question: Gymnosperms (e.g. pines) differ from angiosperms mainly in that gymnosperm seeds are:
options: Not enclosed within an ovary or fruit ('naked seeds')
questions.correct_answer: Not enclosed within an ovary or fruit ('naked seeds')
questions.explanation: Gymnosperm seeds develop exposed, typically on the scales of cones, unlike angiosperm seeds which are enclosed in an ovary that develops into a fruit.

questions.question: 'Alternation of generations' in the life cycle of plants refers to:
options: Alternation between a haploid gametophyte stage and a diploid sporophyte stage
Alternation between day and night growth phases
Alternation between sexual reproduction only in odd years
Alternation between root growth and shoot growth
questions.correct_answer: Alternation between a haploid gametophyte stage and a diploid sporophyte stage
questions.explanation: Plant life cycles alternate between a multicellular haploid (gametophyte) phase that produces gametes and a multicellular diploid (sporophyte) phase that produces spores.

questions.question: Angiosperms are the most diverse and widespread plant group largely because they:
options: Produce flowers and enclosed seeds (fruits), enabling varied strategies for pollination and seed dispersal
Lack vascular tissue, allowing rapid growth
questions.correct_answer: Produce flowers and enclosed seeds (fruits), enabling varied strategies for pollination and seed dispersal
questions.explanation: Flowers and fruits give angiosperms flexible, often co-evolved mechanisms for pollination (by animals, wind) and seed dispersal, contributing to their great diversity.

questions.question: Sponges, simple multicellular animals that lack true tissues and organs, belong to phylum:
questions.explanation: Sponges (Porifera) are sessile aquatic animals with a porous body but no true tissues, organs, or body symmetry in most species.

questions.question: Jellyfish and Hydra possess specialised stinging cells, used for capturing prey and defence, called:
questions.explanation: Cnidarians are named for their cnidocytes, stinging cells containing nematocysts that fire threads to capture prey or deter predators.

questions.question: Flatworms, characterised by a dorsoventrally flattened body and bilateral symmetry, belong to phylum:
questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes (flatworms) includes free-living planarians and parasitic forms such as tapeworms and flukes.

questions.question: Tapeworms, which live as intestinal parasites and absorb nutrients through their body surface, belong to which phylum?
questions.explanation: Tapeworms (class Cestoda) are parasitic flatworms lacking a digestive system; they absorb pre-digested nutrients directly from the host's gut.

questions.question: Roundworms, such as Ascaris, with a cylindrical unsegmented body and a complete digestive tract, belong to phylum:
questions.explanation: Nematodes have a tube-within-a-tube body plan with a complete digestive system, distinguishing them from flatworms.

questions.question: Earthworms, whose bodies are divided into repeating ring-like segments, belong to phylum:
questions.explanation: Annelids are segmented worms; the repeating body segments (metameres) of the earthworm are a defining feature of the phylum.

questions.question: The most species-rich animal phylum, whose members have jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton, is:
questions.explanation: Arthropoda (insects, crustaceans, arachnids, myriapods) is the largest animal phylum, defined by jointed limbs and a hard exoskeleton that is periodically moulted.

questions.question: Snails, octopuses, and clams, despite their very different body forms, are all grouped in phylum:
questions.explanation: Molluscs share a soft body typically featuring a muscular foot, a mantle, and (in many species) a shell, despite great diversity in body form.

questions.question: Starfish and sea urchins, which possess a unique water vascular system and pentaradial (five-part) symmetry as adults, belong to phylum:
questions.explanation: Echinoderms are exclusively marine animals defined by their water vascular system, used for locomotion and feeding, and adult pentaradial symmetry.

questions.question: Which vertebrate class is characterised by dry, scaly skin, internal fertilisation, and being ectothermic ('cold-blooded')?
questions.explanation: Reptiles have dry keratinised scales that reduce water loss, and their body temperature is regulated mainly by external heat sources (ectothermy).

questions.question: Amphibians are distinctive among vertebrates mainly because most species:
options: Undergo metamorphosis, living part of their life cycle in water (e.g. as tadpoles) and part on land as adults
Lay shelled, amniotic eggs on land
Are permanently aquatic and never leave the water
questions.correct_answer: Undergo metamorphosis, living part of their life cycle in water (e.g. as tadpoles) and part on land as adults
questions.explanation: Most amphibians (e.g. frogs) show a dual life history: aquatic, gill-breathing larvae that metamorphose into largely terrestrial, lung-breathing adults.

questions.question: Birds, which are endothermic and covered in feathers, are classified in vertebrate class:
questions.explanation: Aves is the class of warm-blooded, feathered, egg-laying vertebrates that includes all birds.

questions.question: The vertebrate class whose females possess mammary glands to nourish their young with milk is:
questions.explanation: Mammary glands, which produce milk to feed offspring, are a defining feature of class Mammalia.

questions.question: In a food chain, organisms that manufacture their own organic food using sunlight (e.g. green plants) are called:
questions.explanation: Producers (autotrophs) form the base of a food chain by converting light energy into chemical energy stored in organic compounds.

questions.question: The flow of energy through an ecosystem, from producers through successive trophic levels, is best described as:
options: Unidirectional, with energy lost as heat at each transfer between trophic levels
Cyclical, being fully recycled back to producers
Constant at every trophic level, with no losses
Reversible, flowing from consumers back to producers
questions.correct_answer: Unidirectional, with energy lost as heat at each transfer between trophic levels
questions.explanation: Unlike nutrients, energy flows one way through an ecosystem and is progressively lost as metabolic heat, so less energy is available at each successive trophic level.

questions.question: A group of individuals of the same species living in the same area at the same time, capable of interbreeding, is called a:
questions.explanation: A population consists of all members of one species occupying a given area and time, distinguished from a community, which includes multiple species.

questions.question: The non-living, physical and chemical components of an environment, such as temperature, water, and soil pH, are termed:
questions.explanation: Abiotic factors are the non-living physical and chemical conditions of the environment that influence the organisms living there.

questions.question: According to Mendel's Law of Segregation, during gamete formation:
options: The two alleles for a gene separate, so each gamete carries only one allele for that gene
The two alleles for a gene fuse into a single blended allele
Alleles for different genes always segregate together
Only dominant alleles are passed to gametes
questions.correct_answer: The two alleles for a gene separate, so each gamete carries only one allele for that gene
questions.explanation: Mendel's Law of Segregation states that the paired alleles for a trait separate during meiosis, so each gamete receives only one allele of each gene pair.

questions.question: In pea plants, tall (T) is dominant over short (t). If two heterozygous tall plants (Tt x Tt) are crossed, what phenotypic ratio is expected in the offspring?
questions.explanation: A Tt x Tt cross produces genotypes 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt; since T is dominant, TT and Tt are both tall, giving a 3:1 tall-to-short phenotypic ratio.

questions.question: Charles Darwin proposed that evolutionary change occurs mainly through the mechanism of:
questions.explanation: Darwin proposed that individuals with heritable traits better suited to their environment survive and reproduce more successfully, gradually changing the population over generations.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered strong evidence supporting the theory of evolution?
options: The fossil record showing gradual changes in organisms over geological time
The constant, unchanging form of all species throughout history
The absence of any similarities between related species
The complete lack of variation within populations
questions.correct_answer: The fossil record showing gradual changes in organisms over geological time
questions.explanation: The fossil record documents a succession of forms over time, showing transitions and providing direct physical evidence of evolutionary change.
